doc.title: Pete Barbutti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 8, 2022

title: Banned from the Tonight Show for fourteen years
summary: Mel Torme laughing at Pete upstaged Carson, leading to a 14-year ban, then return via guest hosts and a close relationship with Carson.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts

blocks.x: Did you fall afoul of Johnny Carson for a number of years?
Yeah. I did the show in New York, the Tonight Show when it was in New York. That was a long time ago.
And Skitch Henderson was on that.

Skitch Henderson’s band, yeah. And Mel Torme I’m almost certain it was Mel, was on the show and Carson is a big jazz lover and so Mel Torme was a God to him you know. And Mel Torme was on before me, and then they told me, “This is your first shot so you don’t go to the panel, do your stand-up and walk out.” So I did something very hip. Maybe it was the fourth trumpet, I don’t know what I did but Carson actually came and got me physically and took me to the panel. And everybody’s going, “Whoa man, you are made, he’s never done that before.” And we spent a whole segment there and then he said, “Stick around,” and we came back to the next segment and he was telling me short stories and I was telling him some. And Mel Torme, and Mel Torme started to laugh while Carson was telling a story. And Mel didn’t mean anything personally by it but he said, “I’m so sorry John, I didn’t mean to stop your story but I can’t stop laughing at that thing Pete did. And Carson turned like right now it was like how dare you try to be hipper than me. And he ended the segment there and it was 14 years I was not allowed on the Tonight Show. And Peter Lassally, who is the producer, is my biggest fan in the entire world. And yet he would call every once in a while and say, “I’m so sorry I mentioned your name to Johnny and he threw a book on the floor” you know whatever it is. And then Carson started to take time off and they were having guest hosts and John Davidson was the first one. I had worked with John before, we were good buddies. And John asked me on and so I talked to Peter, I said, “Is it okay? I don’t want to get you in trouble here ‘cause you’re my friend.” He said, “No, as long as Carson’s not here.” So I started to do it with all the guest hosts and then one day they called me, and I’d done it like fifty times or something, and one day they called me and said, “Can you do it Friday.” And I said, “Yeah, that’s fine.” And I asked who’s on because if you have a lot of singers I’ll do straight stand-up. If you have a lot of talkers I’ll do something more musical ‘cause if the show is good then I’m good. You know you want the show to be good. The show is the thing. That’s the motto. And so he told me who’s on, and I said, “Who’s hosting?” He said, “Johnny.” I said, “Oh no. I’m on the list, I don’t do it with Johnny.” And the guy said, “Ooh sorry, I didn’t know. I’ll call you next week.” I said okay. Then he called right back and he said, “I just mentioned your name to Carson and he said great.” So I went there, I didn’t apologize, he didn’t apologize, and we started this symbiotic relationship where I would barge into his private make-up room when he was getting make-up and tell him the latest dirty joke, or he’d tell me the latest joke, and we had this thing, and I was one of the very few acts to work that show when they’d say, “What are you going to do” the associate producer would say, “What are you going to do?” And I always tell them, “I’m going to do the poodle joke, I’m going to do the rabbit joke.” And they’d say, “You always say that and you never do that joke.” And I say, “Well I’m going to do it this time.” And they would never ask me to do the joke. Every other comic you had to do
the routine in an office to somebody so they could make sure, the continuity, they could make sure they didn’t have to censor something.
